newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends softer on technical factors.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends softer on technical factors.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 60 basis points at 28.00 percent on Thursday in what traders described as a technical adjustment.
"The spread between overnight government and bank rates was very tight, so demand for government paper surged prior to the close, and that brought rates down," said a trader.
Government and bank rates stood at 28.70 and 29.75 at midsession.
Traders said that U.S. markets being closed for the Thanksgiving holiday, coupled with the forthcoming end of year, made for light trade.
"They've all taken profits, so there's no point in playing the market at this stage. It's best to close the year up and just cover what you need for now," said another trader.
Banco de Mexico injected 7.931 billion pesos into the market by auctioning five credits, which it assigned at between 29.81 percent and 30.24 percent.
Traders had originally estimated a liquidity shortfall of 4.182 billion pesos due to credit maturities, but this was increased by a hefty month-end outflow of liquidity of some three billion pesos.
Credit maturities of 3.005 billion pesos were expected on Friday, and liquidity was expected to be further squeezed by Pemex paying some four billion pesos in taxes.
